title: The kinetics and warm flame chemistry associated with radiative extinction of spherical diffusion flames
summary: Detailed-chemistry transient modelling (UCSD mechanism, 57 species, 270 reactions) of the ISS ethylene spherical flames: as peak temperature falls toward the ~1130 K extinction point, reactant leakage and HO2 chemistry grow; warm-flame chemistry delays but does not prevent extinction. The dissertation version also validates the model against 17 radiatively extinguished ISS normal flames (measured extinction temperature 1130 +/- 23 K vs predicted 1126 +/- 6 K; extinction radius R^2 = 0.98).

items.claim: Warm-flame chemistry delays but does not prevent extinction near 1130 K.
items.quote: At atmospheric pressure, warm flame chemistry is not strong enough to sustain the flame below its extinction point of 1130 K.

items.claim: For 17 normal ISS flames at 1 atm that extinguished radiatively (X_O2 0.20-0.38), thin-filament-pyrometry extinction temperatures averaged 1130 +/- 23 K, against 1126 +/- 6 K from the transient detailed-chemistry model.
items.quote: The means are similar, at 1130 ± 23 K for the experiments and 1126 ± 6 K for the simulations

items.claim: The model predicts the measured flame radius just before radiative extinction for the same 17 flames with R^2 = 0.98.
items.quote: There is good agreement between the model and experiments, with an R2 value of 0.98.

items.claim: Measured burner temperatures are reproduced only if heating of the reactant gas inside the porous sphere is neglected at high flows; burner temperature matters for small flames close to the burner, little for large ones.
items.quote: These results indicate that the temperature of the porous sphere has little effect on the overall flame properties, except in cases where the flame is small and close to the burner.

notes: The journal paper (Combust. Theory Model. 2024) is paywalled; its abstract (WUSTL portal) matches record findings[9]. The open UMD dissertation of the first author (DRUM handle 1903/29996, chapters 2-3) was read instead; it is the dissertation version, so wording may differ from the paper.

title: Soot Formation in Spherical Diffusion Flames
summary: Russian partner team (Frolov et al.) 1-D transient modelling with a soot sub-model of the Flame Design/Adamant normal and inverse ethylene flames at 0.5-2 atm: soot forms where 0.32 < C/O < 0.44 and T > 1300-1500 K.

items.claim: Soot formation window in C/O and temperature, already record findings[10].
items.quote: The results indicate that soot formation in normal and inverse SDFs is concentrated in the region where the local C/O atomic ratio and local temperature satisfy the conditions 0.32 < C/O < 0.44 and T > 1300–1500 K.

notes: MDPI open-access PDF returned HTTP 403 to scripted download; abstract read via OpenAlex/WUSTL. Modelling paper; the record already cites it.

title: On the existence of steady-state gaseous microgravity spherical diffusion flames in the presence of radiation heat loss
summary: ISS experiments and transient modelling show steady spherical flames can exist with radiative loss if the steady size is below the radiative-extinction size and the flame develops before cooling below 1130 K; steady flames were observed for up to 870 s.

items.claim: Conditions for steady flames and 870 s burns.
items.quote: Despite a narrow range of attainable conditions, flames that exhibit steady-state behavior are observed aboard the ISS for up to 870 s, even with the constraint of a finite boundary.

notes: Elsevier accepted manuscript blocked (HTTP 403); NTRS lists it with no download. Abstract from the WUSTL research portal; identical to the text in the PSI final report.

title: Critical temperature and reactant mass flux for radiative extinction of ethylene microgravity spherical diffusion flames at 1 bar
summary: ISS normal and inverse ethylene flames at 1 bar all extinguish at a critical 1130 K and a critical reactant flux (0.2 g/m^2/s fuel, 0.68 g/m^2/s O2); a simple equation gives flame size at extinction from the reactant flow.

items.claim: Critical extinction temperature and fluxes.
items.quote: Despite this broad range of conditions, all flames extinguish at a critical extinction temperature of 1130 K, and a fuel-based mass flux of 0.2 g/m 2 -s for normal flames, and an oxygen-based mass flux of 0.68 g/m 2 -s for inverse flames.

notes: Full text blocked (Elsevier, HTTP 403; NTRS record has no download). Abstract from WUSTL portal. The extinction-size equation itself is still not quoted (see record gaps).

title: Observations of long duration microgravity spherical diffusion flames aboard the International Space Station
summary: First ISS Flame Design results: normal ethylene flames at 1 atm grew monotonically, burned 28-336 s, cooled and extinguished radiatively, sometimes after oscillating partial extinction; small flames were quasi-steady until the burner temperature limit.

items.claim: Burn times, growth and radiative extinction.
items.quote: Burn times range from 28 – 336 s. All flames grow monotonically after ignition.

items.claim: Small flames quasi-steady, limited by burner heating.
items.quote: Sufficiently small flames with low radiation losses exhibit quasi-steady behavior, but burner heating is significant, and the experimental duration is dictated by the temperature limit of the porous sphere.

title: The effects of elevated pressure on the kinetics and extinction of hot, warm, and cool gaseous ethylene spherical diffusion flames
summary: ISS round-2 tests at 0.5-3 bar with TFP: extinction temperature falls with pressure; at 3 bar the flame passes below 1130 K into the warm-flame regime. In the dissertation, three inverse flames (85% O2 burner stream into 10% C2H4, 3.41 mg/s O2) at 0.5, 1 and 3 atm: 0.5 and 1 atm extinguish at similar temperatures, 3 atm about 50 K lower (the abstract says almost 60 K). Simulations at 50 bar give a long warm flame and then a cool flame.

items.claim: Extinction temperature of ISS ethylene flames decreases with pressure; at 3 bar it falls below 1130 K into the warm-flame regime.
items.quote: Experimental results show that increasing the pressure from 1 atm to 3 atm decreased the ethylene extinction temperature by almost 60 K.

items.claim: Test conditions and size of the pressure effect: three inverse flames identical except pressure; 0.5 and 1 atm extinguish at similar temperature, 3 atm roughly 50 K lower.
items.quote: Flame A and C extinguish at similar temperatures, but Flame B extinguishes roughly 50 K lower.
items.locator: Waddell 2023 UMD dissertation, sec. 4.3.1, Table 4.1, Fig. 4.1

items.claim: Simulation at 50 atm: warm-flame chemistry extends the burn by over 500 s, then the flame settles as a cool flame.
items.quote: At 50 atm the flame was able to extend its burn time by over 500 s due to the emergence of warm flame chemistry.

notes: Journal paper (Proc. Combust. Inst. 40, 2024) blocked (Elsevier HTTP 403; NTRS accepted manuscript has no download). Its abstract is on the WUSTL portal; the experimental detail was read in the first author's open UMD dissertation (chapter 4). The dissertation gives two values for the 1-3 atm drop (almost 60 K in the abstract, roughly 50 K in sec. 4.3.1).
